title: HDFC Bank Shares Rise as RBI Approves LIC Stake Hike to 9.99%
excerpt: India's largest insurer can now more than double its holding in the country's biggest private-sector bank, with the approval valid for one year.
body:
• RBI has approved Life Insurance Corporation's application to raise its stake in HDFC Bank from 4.11% to up to 9.99% of paid-up share capital
  • HDFC Bank shares advanced about 1% following the announcement, as markets view the potential LIC buying as a vote of confidence in India's largest private-sector lender
  • Under RBI regulations, any entity acquiring 5% or more of a bank's shares needs prior central bank approval; LIC's potential purchase could be worth thousands of crores

RBI Greenlights LIC's Stake Hike

The Reserve Bank of India has approved Life Insurance Corporation of India's (LIC) application to increase its aggregate holding in HDFC Bank to up to 9.99% of the bank's paid-up share capital or voting rights, HDFC Bank disclosed in a stock exchange filing.

LIC currently holds a 4.11% stake in India's largest private-sector bank by market capitalization. The RBI approval clears the way for the state-owned insurer to more than double its holding, potentially acquiring an additional 5.88 percentage points worth of shares.

HDFC Bank shares responded positively, advancing roughly 1% in trading following the announcement.

Why the Approval Matters

Under RBI's Master Direction on Acquisition and Holding of Shares in Banking Companies, any entity seeking to acquire 5% or more of a bank's paid-up capital—classified as \"major shareholding\"—must obtain prior regulatory approval. LIC's current 4.11% stake sits just below that threshold, meaning any significant open-market purchases would have required this clearance.

The approval is typically valid for one year, during which LIC can accumulate shares up to the 9.99% ceiling. The 9.99% cap is a regulatory limit—not a mandate. LIC faces no penalty if it chooses not to increase its holding to that level, but it cannot exceed it.

HDFC Bank, valued at over $150 billion, is India's most widely held bank stock, with institutional investors across the globe holding significant positions. LIC's potential buying activity could provide meaningful price support.

LIC's Track Record as an Anchor Investor

LIC is India's largest domestic institutional investor, managing a portfolio that stretches across equities, bonds, and real estate. The insurer has historically used its deep pockets to stabilize markets during periods of heavy foreign portfolio investor (FPI) selling, and its entries into large-cap banking stocks are closely watched by market participants.

\"LIC is unquestionably a sentimental booster for HDFC Bank stockholders.\"

— Mohit Gulati, CIO and Managing Partner, ITI Growth Opportunities Fund

The timing is notable. HDFC Bank's share price has been under pressure as the banking sector navigates tighter liquidity conditions and a post-merger integration period. LIC's vote of confidence signals that India's largest insurer sees value at current levels.

Implications for NRI Investors

HDFC Bank is one of the most widely held Indian stocks among overseas investors, including NRIs with direct equity portfolios and mutual fund holdings. The bank trades as an ADR on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker HDB, making it directly accessible to US-based investors.

LIC's approved stake hike could support the stock through a period of broader market uncertainty. The approval also reflects the RBI's comfort with higher domestic institutional ownership in India's systemically important banks, a trend that has accelerated since the HDFC Ltd.–HDFC Bank merger in 2023 expanded the bank's share capital substantially.

The RBI's approval is subject to compliance with provisions of the Banking Regulation Act, SEBI regulations, and the Foreign Exchange Management Act. LIC must ensure its aggregate holding does not exceed 9.99% at any time.

Market Context

The announcement comes as Indian banking stocks face a mixed backdrop. The RBI held the repo rate steady at 5.25% in its August policy meeting, maintaining a neutral stance as it balances growth support against inflation vigilance. Durable liquidity in the banking system has increased by about ₹1.2 lakh crore since June, partly driven by FCNR(B) deposit inflows and government spending.

For HDFC Bank specifically, analysts note the bank's long-term fundamentals remain strong despite near-term margin pressure from the post-merger deposit base adjustment. LIC's willingness to accumulate shares at current valuations suggests the insurer agrees with that assessment.
